Commentary.Commentary: That unsettled the visitors and the ball getting softer helped England's cause. The duo stitched a 50-run stand. Though Moeen fell, Curran mixed caution with aggression to perfection. He shepherded the tail smartly and scored a gutsy fifty, just the way he did in the first Test at Edgbaston. India will be ruing the fact that they didn't capitalize when they had the home side staring down the barrel. They have a tricky phase of around 20 minutes to play out. England will be aiming to make some early inroads. Join us shortly.

The duo of Bumrah and Sharma was relentless and didn't allow the Englishmen to get any sort of momentum. The move to promote Bairstow to No. 4 didn't work either. Shami bowled a fierce first spell as well and picked up two quick wickets. After that, Ali and Curran got together and played some shots.

A terrific display with the bat from Sam Curran has helped England to put up a decent total on the board. Considering that they were 86/6 and that they almost reached the 250-run mark, deserves credit. Earlier, things were not rosy for the hosts though. After winning the toss and choosing to bat, their top order was found wanting against some penetrative Indian pace bowling.

OUT! Bowled 'em! Tossed up ball on middle and off, Curran clears his front leg and tries to slog it across the line but misses to get his stumps shattered. A top knock from him though. ENGLAND ARE BOWLED OUT FOR 246!
Slower through the air, defended towards mid off.
Bye! Down the leg side, Anderson tries to put bat on ball but misses. Pant fails to collect it as well and a single is taken.
Floated around off, Anderson comes forward and blocks it.
Ashwin is back.
Smart choice from Bumrah! Dug in short by him, Curran ducks under it. Anderson has to survive the next over.
Full length ball attacking the stumps, Sam comes ahead and defends it calmly.
In the arc but not out of the park! Fuller length ball, angling in, Curran backs away and tries to send this out of Southampton but misses.
Short of a length ball on off, kept out watchfully.

Sent back by Anderson! Back of a length ball outside off, Curran glides it to third man and starts haring across to the other end. He looks at James and the No 11 has his hand up. Sam turns back and reaches his crease. Anderson has a smile on his face and Curran smiles back.
On a length outside off, dabbed towards point.
He survives! Shortish ball down the leg side, James moves inside the line and evades it.
Back of a length ball, Anderson gets behind it and defends it nicely.
The batsman works it down the leg side. The batsmen have run through for a single. Anderson has two balls to survive. Can he do so?
FOUR! Straight as an arrow! Full ball on middle, Curran lifts it over the bowler for a boundary.
Back of a length ball outside off, Sam shuffles across and tries to work it to the leg side but misses.
Short ball, Curran ducks under it.
James Anderson is the last man in.

OUT! The change of bat has led to doom for Broad! Jasprit Bumrah has provided the much-needed breakthrough for India and he lets out a grunt. He steams in from around the wicket and bowls a good length ball around off. It hits the deck and comes with the natural angle as Broad is late to bring his bat down in time and is hit in front of the wickets. The visitors appeal in unison and the umpire raises the dreaded finger. Stuart was beaten for pace there. The 63-run stand from 57 balls has been nipped in the bud. It has given England what they needed though.
Hardik Pandya has something to advice to Bumrah. Meanwhile, there is a change of bat for Broad.
Good running! On a length on middle, Curran taps it to mid off and scurries to the other end.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. They pick up a single.
On a length on off, Curran looks to tap and run by trying to play it towards point but gets an inside edge onto his pads. Eventually, the ball rolls to the same area and the batsmen cross.
FOUR! Going from bad to worse for India! Their shoulders are dropping. Short and asking for trouble, Curran stands tall and slaps it behind point for a rocketing boundary.

There is no one in the deep, Curran continues to flourish. Slower ball from Bumrah on middle and leg. Curran is foxed and is early into his shot. Ends up chipping it down the ground and comes back for a brace.
Jasprit Bumrah returns.
On a length on middle and leg, Broad wants to help it away but is struck on the thigh pad.
Similar ball outside off, flayed away again to the same region for a single.
Width on offer outside off, Broad slices it uppishly towards deep backward point for a run.
Sprays this one down the leg side, Broad tries to put bat on ball but only connects with thin air.
Better from Shami. He hits the deck hard and bowls a well-directed bouncer. Broad sways away awkwardly to evade it.
Nothing is working for India at the moment! Full ball on off, Curran attempts to hit it down the ground but gets a thick inside edge down towards fine leg. A run taken.
Mohammed Shami returns.
Makes use of the depth of the crease to clip it away through square leg for a single.
Surprise bouncer from Pandya, Curran fails to hook it away.

Short of a length outside off, flayed away through point for three runs. The 50-run stand has come between the two and that too only in 43 balls. A brilliant counter-attack this has been. The English camp is all smiles.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They manage to come back for the second.
Smart from Sam! He moves inside the line to the good length ball and works it away to deep backward square leg for a couple.
Finally Pant collects one! Down the leg side, Sam fails to tickle it away. The keeper moves to his right and takes it nicely.
FOUR! Streaky but they all count! Broad leans ahead to defend but gets an outside edge. Rahane at first slip is a bit late to react and the ball goes past him to the fence.
Tossed up around off, eased off the front foot to mid off.
Almost a replica of the previous delivery as it is pushed to mid off again.
Full ball around off, driven crisply to the man at mid off.
Driven towards the mid off region.

Not Out! Yes, the impact has saved Broad. Coming in with the arm, Stuart comes ahead to defend it but misses to get pinged on the pads. Ashwin appeals vociferously but the umpire thinks otherwise. The keeper is convinced and Kohli listens to him to signal the 'T'. Time for the replays. There is nothing on the Snicko. The Hawk Eye rolls in and the impact is just outside off. The ball just brushed the front pad before hitting the back pad. That was taken into account by the third umpire.

Time for the review! It is regarding an LBW appeal against Stuart Broad. Pant is really confident and suggests his skipper to take the review which he agrees to. The point of impact might save the batsman.
Short ball, Curran pulls it in front of square leg for a couple. 11 from this one, 23 from the last two.
Runs are coming thick and fast now! Broad swings at a length ball outside off and gets it overs covers. Three runs taken.
In the air... but safe! Full ball attacking the stumps, Broad chips it but mistimes it over wide mid on. It is in no man's land and the batsmen take a couple.

Four Leg Byes! The extras count has moved to 33, shoddy stuff from India. Down the leg side, Broad tries to glance it but the ball brushes his pads and goes past the diving Pant once again to the ropes.
Beaten! On a length, leaving Stuart. He fishes at it and misses.
Good length ball on off, Broad hangs back and blocks it stoutly.
Double change. Hardik Pandya is back for a burst.
Quicker in pace on middle and leg, played off the inner half towards the man at 45. 12 from the over.
FOUR! These are handy runs for England. Coming in with the arm, Curran clears his front leg, lines it up and drags his heave through mid-wicket to find the fence.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Edged but safe! Floated around off, Curran pushes at it but gets an outside edge past the slip fielder. A couple taken.

SIX! What a way to get to his second Test fifty! This young lad certainly packs a punch and has a matured head on his young shoulders. Kneels to the tossed up ball and whacks it over long on for a maximum. He has helped England make a comeback, being the chief architect behind it. The 200 also comes up for England.
Full ball on middle and leg, going down. Curran tries to flick it away but is hit on the pads.
Drinks! Last one of the day. Meanwhile, Ravichandran Ashwin comes back for a bowl.
Back of a length ball on the hips of Broad who stands tall and bunts it down.
On a good length on the pads of Broad who works it to the leg side.
Hangs back and defends this ball in front of him.
Broad shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Outside off again, left alone.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Stays inside his crease and is happy to give Broad the strike for the next over.

FOUR! SHOT! Curran moves to 47! The young teen once again taking the game away from the Indians. Sharma corrects his length by bowling it too far outside off. Curran uses his fast hands and cuts it through point for a boundary.
Four Byes! Oh dear! Pant hides his face. Bad line from Sharma. Bowls this down the leg side again, too far for Curran to flick it. Pant runs and dives to his right. And just like before, to no-avail.
Similar ball. On a good length on middle and leg. Broad goes back but does not get bat to it. They steal another leg bye.
Length ball on middle and leg, Broad hops and looks to tuck it away. Misses it to get hit on his thigh pad.
Outside off, easy leave for Broad.
Full and down leg. Broad cannot get bat to ball. Hits his leg and goes away from the fielder to the on side. They pinch a single. The umpire signals Leg Bye.
The batsman opens the face of the bat and helps it to third man. They pick up a single.

Four Byes! Make that 18 byes for the innings. Another one of those full pitched ball down the leg side. Curran is late in getting his bat down and loses his complete balance. Pant jumps to his right but the ball evades him. Has a smirk on his face as he knows he can't do anything about it.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Driven by Curran to the cover region.

Comes in from over the wicket and serves it outside off. Curran looks to go after it but cannot make any contact. India will have to be wary of Curran. He will look to tee off with the tail like he did at Edgbaston.
Broad survives. Gets behind the ball and sees it off.
Curran gets behind the ball and hits it to the off side. Gives Broad one ball to face.
Inside edge but safe. Length ball on middle and leg. Broad gets an inside edge and the ball goes towards the on side. Away from the fielder which enables them to cross.
Stuart Broad is the new man in.

OUT! Ishant gets his man! No reviews left for England and Rashid has to walk back. Ishant serves this full on middle and leg. The ball moves in the air and comes in after pitching. Rashid is caught on his back foot trying to flick the ball. Misses it and gets hit on his pads. The Indians appeal and the umpire takes his time in raising his finger. Sadly for England, the replay shows that would have gone to miss the leg stump.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball - but fails.
Bangs it a tad short. Rashid hops and just tickles it away through fine leg. The fielder in the deep mops it up and keeps it to two.
Stays inside and drives this ball towards the bowler.
Runs in from over the wicket and lands it with an angle around off. Sam is solid in defense.
Length ball around off, well blocked.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Length ball around off. It nips back into Rashid who looks to hit it to the on side. Gets extra bounce which hits him on his glove. The ball goes to the off side and they cross.
Full outside off, Rashid leaves it alone.
Jasprit Bumrah in for another spell.
Pitches it up again. Outside off. Curran plays it with soft hands towards mid off and thinks of the run. A loud NO from his partner and they decide against it.
Good looking shot but straight to the man. Length ball moving away from Curran. He drives it superbly but to the man at short point.
Good length ball from over the wicket. Lands it around off, Curran bunts it down.
Nicely timed! Another full ball on middle and off. Rashid flicks it through mid-wicket. The man in the deep keeps it to just one.
Inswinger. Served full around off, the ball moves in the air. Rashid gets behind it and drives it along the turf.
Full and in line of the stumps, Curran opens the bat face and helps it to deep backward point for a run.
Full and on the pads, flicked away to square leg.
Finds the gap this time, punches this through covers to give his partner the strike.
Short ball outside off, Curran pulls it but finds the man at mid-wicket.
Rocks back and cuts this ball towards cover-point.
Stands tall and punches this ball for the mid off fielder to collect.
Darts this on the pads of Curran who plays it to the bowler with a straight bat.

A big shout for an LBW falls on deaf ears! Full ball on off, swinging in like a banana. Adil Rashid falls over a bit as he fails to flick it and is struck on the pads. Ishant and Co rise up but the umpire shakes his head. Perhaps, that was doing too much.

Well played and well fielded! Full and too straight, Rashid flicks it nonchalantly through square leg. Shikhar Dhawan in the deep hares across to his left and dives full length to keep the ball in play. It is checked upstairs. The replay shows that he is fine.
Stump-to-stump line, Rashid camps back and answers it with a straight bat.
Edged but no harm done! Good length ball around off, straightening after landing to square Rashid up. He tries to block it but gets an outside edge which falls short of the gully fielder.
Ishant hits the deck hard around the off stump channel. Adil gets behind the line and blocks it solidly.
Fuller in length on middle and leg, tucked around the corner for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Short one this time on middle and leg, Curran pulls it through mid-wicket for a run.

Ashwin floats this around off. It's the off spinner. Curran covers the stumps and looks to pad this from outside off. The ball hits his pad and goes towards the slip region. Stifled appeal but nothing from the umpire. The ball was probably not coming in enough with the arm.
Adil Rashid comes out to bat. We all know he has the ability. Can he support Sam Curran and take England past 200?

OUT! Finally! India break the 81-run stand and get closer to wrapping up England. Ashwin tosses this up around off. Ali gets low on his knee and looks to slog sweep this away but gets beaten by the loop on it. Ends up getting a top edge to it. The ball balloons towards square leg where Bumrah makes a lot of ground to his left and takes a good diving catch. Ali misses out on his 50 but has helped the cause of his side.
Moeen flicks it away with a wristy shot.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

Four Byes! Another one of those takes for the keeper! England is not a good place to keep. Sharma serves this down the leg side. Curran looks to flick it but does not make any contact. Pant once again dives to his right but cannot get glove to it. Boundary towards the fine leg region.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Teased! Full and wide outside off. Curran who is supposed to leave that one goes for it but does not make any contact.
Class! Doesn't go to the boundary but some confident stroke making from Curran. Another short ball outside off, Curran cuts it uppishly through point for two more runs.
Drags his length back on the similar line, Curran punches it towards mid off.
Fuller ball around off, Curran defends it getting behind the ball.
Ishant Sharma has been called back into the attack.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Short again around off, Sam punches this through covers to rotate strike.
FOUR! Brilliant from Curran! The pitch has eased out now and Curran is making the most of it. Short ball outside off, sits up nicely for Sam who cuts it through point for a boundary.
Pitched up ball around off, Curran drives it towards covers.
Comes ahead and hits the ball towards the bowler.
Tossed up ball around off, Curran hits it to the off side.
Moeen chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Four Byes! What is Pant supposed to do with that? Nothing. Shami comes in from round the wicket and lands this on the leg stump. It pitches and swings away with the angle. Ali leaves it alone, Pant dives to his right but can't get anywhere close to it. The ball runs to the fine leg boundary.
Play and miss. Length ball around off, Ali looks to drive it but makes contact with thin air.
Around off, Ali blocks it well.
Outside off, left alone.
SC drives this through the covers.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

NOT OUT! Always looked like it was sliding down but India just for the sake of it, take it up. Ashwin gives this air around off. It comes in sharply with the arm and hits Sam on his back leg who is forward in defense. The players appeal in unison but the umpire stays put. After a long wait, Kohli reviews it. The replays show the ball would have clipped the leg stump. Umpire's call so India don't lose their review.
Review time! Kohli has taken an LBW decision up against Sam Curran. Looks like it's going wide.
Comes forward and plays this into the ground.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Off spinner outside off, Curran covers his stumps and leaves it alone.
A bit short outside off, Curran reaches for it and cuts it through point to retain the strike.
Drags his length back, Sam goes back and punches it to the off side.
Changes his length by pitching it up. Curran drives it to mid off.
Beauty! Skids through after pitching. Good length ball outside off, Curran feels for it but does not connect.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Covers his stumps and defends the ball from the crease.
Good leave. Reads the spin again and is confident in what he is doing. This one is just outside off. Goes straight after pitching and Ali watches it go through.
Ashwin bowls this fuller outside off, Ali bunts it down.
SIX! Huge! Full of confidence is Moeen! Reads the ball from Ashwin's hand. Steps down the track to this off spinner and smokes it over long on for a biggie.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Easy. Loopy ball in line of the stumps, Ali plays it with a straight bat.
Hangs back and milks this through mid on for an easy single.
Good ball from Shami. Darts it full on middle, Ali is late but does well to get bat to it.
Full and around off, Ali is solid in defense.
Nice. Gets behind the ball and places the ball in the gap towards square leg for a brace.
Pitches it up again, this time around off. Curran looks to tap it to the off side but gets a french cut which goes past the leg stump. They cross.
Full again on middle and leg, Curran turns his bat to the on side.
Comes in from over the wicket and lands it full on that leg stump area. Ali flicks it away towards deep square leg to change ends.
Mohammed Shami to bowl from the other end.
Sam has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. .
Tossed up ball around off, Curran gets behind the ball and sees it off.
Goes back again and stonewalls this ball in front of him.
Rocks back and pushes the ball towards covers for an easy run.
Gives this air outside off, Moeen leans ahead and bunts it ahead.

The players walk out after a warm cup of tea. The two left-handers in Moeen Ali and Sam Curran, who just crossed a 50-run stand will look to bat for as long as possible. India will continue with Ravi Ash. A slip and short leg for him. Let's go!
... Day 1, Session 3...

However, some brave cricket and smart counter-attacking batting from both, Sam Curran and Moeen Ali, has seen England steady the ship a bit. There is still a lot of work for them to do though. India, on the other hand, would want to break this stand and clean up the tail as quickly as possible. Join us on the other side of the break.

Session highlights - 27 overs, 82 runs, 2 wickets. If the first session was dominated by the tourists, it can be said that this one belonged to England. The visitors continued to be on a roll after the break as Mohammed Shami removed Joss Buttler and Ben Stokes rather quickly.

England's intensity is on show here. It's the last ball before the break and what do they do? They take a cheeky single. Shami keeps it just back of a length around off, Ali defends it from the crease and calls for a run. Curran responds well and they complete a good single. THAT'S TEA ON DAY 1!
A fullish delivery on off is driven to mid off and they cross over quickly for a single.
Curran comes forward and defends this full and straight ball.

Beaten! Shami is giving it his all but the edges are just not being found. He keeps it on a length just outside off. Curran tries to put bat on ball but misses as the ball beats his outside edge by a whisker.
Shami fires it on Ali's pads on just a back of a length. Ali stays back and flicks it to the deep square leg region. A run taken.

Chance of a run out for India? Shami bowls it fuller on the middle stump line. Curran stays back and defends it with a straight bat and takes off. The ball goes towards Ashwin at mid off who runs in, picks it up cleanly and underarms it to the non-striker's end but misses the stumps as Curran is seen diving inside the crease. The replay shows that he just made the crease before the ball passed the stumps. That brings up the 50-run stand between the duo. They need to keep it up.
Shami is back for the final over before Tea.
This full pitched ball on off is driven to the cover fielder.
Slower through the air on the off stump, Ali comes forward and defends.
This tossed up delivery just outside off is driven towards the cover region and the batsmen exchange strike.
Bowls it a bit straighter on the leg stump line, Ali goes back and turns it around towards the deep square leg region for a single.
Tossed up on middle and leg. Ali blocks it out.
Ashwin starts off with a full  floated delivery outside off. Ali shoulders arms.
Again down the leg side from Bumrah. Curran looks to get something on it but misses once again.
Short of a length ball around off, defended.
On a length down the leg stump, Curran misses the flick.
Fuller ball around middle and off, it swings away from Curran who does well to get behind the line to defend it.
On the hips, tucked to fine leg for a run.
Ali chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Tossed up on off, the ball pitches and turns away. Curran comes forward, smothers the spin and defends.
Tossed up around off, Curran guides it towards the point region.
Ashwin misses his line and strays on Curran's pads, but the batsman keeps it out by defending.

Risky! Curran sees the flight on this floated delivery on off, takes a few steps down the tack and tries to go over mid off. He is unable to get under the ball and hence does not get enough elevation. But it works in his favor as the ball is lofted in the air for a short while but falls short of the mid off fielder. The Indians with their hands on their heads.
Punched off the back foot by the batsman.
Tossed up ball on the off stump is defended off the front foot by Curran.
Beaten! Good comeback by Bumrah but he is unlucky not to get the edge. Keeps this again on a length on off. Moves away on pitching and also beats the outside edge of Ali's bat.

SIX! Ali goes for the hook and gets rewarded with a maximum. They say luck favors the brave and Ali and Curran are playing some brave cricket here. Bumrah bangs this one short, Ali goes back, swivels and goes for the hook. The ball gets the top edge and flies towards the fine leg region. The fielder at fine leg is a bit square but it would not have mattered as the ball sails over the ropes. These are some important runs for the hosts.
A back of a length delivery on off, Ali rocks back and keeps it out.
Well played by Curran. This one is kept on a length on the off stump line. But this one comes in after landing. Curran does well to account for the inward movement and drives it to mid off.
Keeps it a bit fuller and straighter. Curran does well to block it out.
Bumrah starts the new over with a back of a length delivery on off. Curran decides to leave it as the ball flies across him into Pant's gloves.
A bit wider of off, Ali shoulders arms.
Tossed up ball on the off stump, Ali comes forward and keeps it out.
A very full delivery wide of the off stump, Ali goes for the drive away from his body, gets an inside edge and the ball rolls back to the bowler's left.
Floated delivery outside off, Ali leaves it alone.
Tossed up ball on off, defended down.
Ashwin keeps it on the middle and off line but the length is a bit shorter than his liking, Curran goes back and turns this one around the corner to pick up a single.

A jaffa! A short of a length ball going away from Ali. He looks to have a go at it from his crease but gets beaten. The slip cordon is showing some excitement but Bumrah has a smirk  and he nods in disagreement. Brilliant over from the youngster once again.

Skiddy! Similar delivery to the one bowled to Jennings in the morning. Ali does well to get behind the line of the in swinger and keep it out. Though the ball has gone softer, Bumrah is still making it talk.
A touch too straight this time and enough for Curran to work it around the corner for another easy single.
Similar kind of delivery from Bumrah. Curran gets around the delivery to defend it.
On a length around middle and off, blocked.
Short ball targeting the grille of Moeen who swivels and gets it to deep backward square leg for a run.
A bit more flight on this one, tempting Curran into the drive and the southpaw drives it straight to the man at mid off.
Curran comes forward and defends this floated delivery off the front foot.
A tossed up delivery on off is defended back to the bowler.
Keeps it a bit shorter on off, Curran goes back and punches towards the covers region.

Edge found but he's safe. Ashwin slows this one down a bit and lands it on a fuller length around middle and off. Curran is not forward nor back and tries to block it away. The ball pitches and turns away taking the outside edge. But the edge flies far away from the fielder at first slip and he had no chance.
Tossed up ball on the stumps is pushed back to the bowler.
A fuller length ball on off, Ali defends it off the front foot.

Beaten! Ali is lucky again as this one misses his outside edge by a whisker. Bumrah lands it in the corridor around off and gets it to move away on pitching. Ali tries to get bat on ball but gets beaten.
Bowls this one a bit straight, in line of the stumps. Ali, from within his crease, flicks it away to square leg.
Similar delivery and a similar response as Ali leaves this length ball outside off.
Outside off again by Bumrah and Ali shoulders arms.
Starts the over with a short of a length ball around off, angling away, Ali leaves it alone.
Tossed up around off, Curran prods forward and blocks.
Curran punches this one towards the cover region as Ashwin pulls back the length a bit.
Floats this one a bit fuller on off, Curran elegantly drives it to mid off.
Tossed up on middle, defended off the front foot.
A similar ball is played in a similar way by the other batsman. Ali flicks this floated delivery into the leg side for a single.
Tossed up on his pads, Curran flicks it away towards mid-wicket to pick up a single.
Ashwin comes back into the attack.

Beaten! Peach from Bumrah. Lands this one on a length around the middle and off line, Ali is tempted to poke at it. The ball moves away on landing and beats Ali's outside edge. A wonderful ball to end the over.
FOUR! Bumrah misses his line and length by a bit and Ali pounces on it. Keeps this a bit shorter and a bit wide of off. Ali cuts it and cuts it superbly to find the gap in the point region.
On a length just outside off, Ali does well to watchfully let it go behind.
This one is too wide to entice Ali into a stroke.
A bit fuller and a bit wider of off, Ali shoulders arms.
A bit shorter and in the line of the stumps. Ali leaves this one on length as the ball whizzes over the middle stump.
Jasprit Bumrah returns.
A back of a length delivery is defended back to the bowler.

FOUR! Third boundary in the over! Short of a length just outside off, Curran goes for the cut, beats the man at point and also the one at deep point for the ball to race across for a boundary. Curran counter-attacking here. Some smart batting.
Length ball outside off is left alone.

Beaten! A loose ball is followed by a loose shot. Pandya keeps it short and way wide of off, Curran tries his best to reach to the ball but misses it completely. On a different day it could have taken the edge and would have looked a very silly dismissal.

Super timing from Curran. Pandya drops it a bit short and wide of off, Curran stays back and punches it through the point region. The man at the deep point boundary slides and stops it from crossing the ropes and saves two.

FOUR! Brilliant batting by Curran. Pandya overcompensates and lands it very full. Curran comes forward, leans a bit and drives it straight down the ground past the bowler's right. The ball goes past the boundary and Curran is adding some vital runs for the home team.
FOUR! Cracked! Pandya lands this one short and wide outside off. Curran rocks back and cuts this one in the gap between covers and point. The timing is exquisite and the ball races across the fence.
Ali will feel he's missed out on it. Shami bowls it very full and wide outside off. Ali leans forward and square drives it, however, finds the fielder at point.
Bumper from Shami. Ali ducks under it.
A length ball outside off is left alone.

FOUR! Streaky! But as they say, it's not how, but how many in cricket. Shami keeps it a bit shorter in length around off, Ali stands within his crease and pushes at it tentatively. The ball pitches and moves away taking the thick outside edge of Ali's bat and the ball flies through the vacant gully region to the boundary. England's 100 comes up.
A length ball around off, Ali comes forward and defends it.
A shorter and wider delivery outside off is punched off the back foot towards the point region, Ali finds the gap and the batsman take a brace.
Hangs back to the short of a length ball and blocks it out.
Streaky but effective! Fullish ball around off, Ali just keeps his bat down to block it but gets an outside edge past gully. Three more is the result.
This is good batting from Curran! In the slot for him, he leans ahead confidently and drives it past the diving Rahane. Ample time for the batsmen to come back for the third run.
Well outside off, Sam has no need to go after it and he doesn't.
Brilliant piece of fielding from Rahane! Back of a length outside off, Curran punches it nicely towards covers. Ajinkya moves to his left and dives like a goalkeeper to stop a certain boundary.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Hardik Pandya is back.

That was so risky! Shami can't believe it that it missed the off pole. Coming in sharply from outside off, Moeen lets it through and it just misses the stumps. Mohammed has his hands on his head and a wry smile on his face.
Outside off, left alone.
Beautiful bowling from Shami! He steams in from around the wicket and swings the ball in. At the very last moment, it pitches and moves away. Ali has to play at it and is beaten all ends up.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.

That was poor from Moeen! Short and there is room on offer, he chases it away from his body and almost nicks it behind. You got to have your concentrations levels right up when the ball is doing so much.
Good length ball in the fifth stump channel, Ali points his bat skywards to let it go.
Time for Drinks!
Sharma drags his length back a touch. Sam camps back and presents a water-tight defense.
In the zone outside off, Curran points his bat skywards to allow it through.
Sharma continues to be full around the off stump channel. Curran without much foot movement goes for a flashy drive but gets it off the inner half towards mid off.
Nicely played! We have seen in the past that he is good on the drive. Fractionally overpitched outside off, Sam leans ahead and caresses it through covers. A couple taken.

Well bowled! That surprised Curran a bit. Very full ball on middle and off, there is some movement in the air. Curran loses a bit of balance but manages to just keep it out down the track. Ishant tumbles down on his followthrough and stops it.
On a length around off, Curran camps back and stonewalls it.
Shami bangs this one in short. Ali sees it early and ducks under it.
Keeps it on a length around the off stump, Curran defends by getting behind the line of the ball.
Sam Curran comes out to bat. Can he deliver on his return?

OUT! Three reds and there goes England's best all-rounder. Even the review couldn't save him and in turn, Stokes couldn't save the review either. Shami's consistent line and length gets rewarded. He lands this one on a length just outside off, angling in from around the wicket. Stokes gets across and tries to keep it out but the ball pitches and sharply nips into the southpaw. It beats the inside edge and raps him on his front pad. The Indian players appeal and the umpire obliges. Stokes though feels he has a chance to get away with this one. He decides to challenge the decision. The Snicko doesn't detect any spike. Time for the Hawk Eye. It shows the ball is hitting in line and is crashing into the stumps. Stokes is a dead duck and what's more, England have lost both their reviews now.
A review for LBW is taken by England. The man in question is Stokes. It looks very close.
Shami keeps it wide of off stump and Stokes has nothing to do with it.
Shami gets straighter and Ali flicks it to the deep fine leg region. They exchange strike.

Absolute beauty! Beats him on the very first delivery of the over. Shami fires in an 88 mph delivery on a length just outside off. What's more, it moves away on landing. Ali, from within the crease, looks to block it but the movement beats his bat and Ali survives.
Good to see Mohammed Shami back on the ground and raring to go.
A fuller one this time just outside off, but the line is not close enough to tempt Stokes into a shot.
A bit wider of off this time, Stokes leaves.
Sharma strays on Ali's pads who flicks it away to deep fine leg for a single.
Stokes walks down the track, may be to negate the movement. Ishant keeps it a bit shorter of a length. Stokes taps it away towards the cover-point region and picks up yet another single.
Ishant is not leaving that channel. He's just not giving anything away here. Probing away again on a length just outside off. Stokes does well to watchfully let it go.

In the last over, Mohammed Shami was struck hard in his followthrough. He is sitting near the boundary ropes now, being attended to by the physio. He looks in a lot of pain. Let's hope it is nothing serious.
Ishant continues to keep it on a length around off stump. Stokes gets forward and defends.
Shami attacks the line of the stumps and keeps it a bit fuller. Stokes turns it towards mid-wicket and picks up a single.
A length ball around off is pushed towards the cover region.
Full and straight again, Driven to mid off.

Beaten! Shami gets his line and length right this time. Lands it in the corridor around off, Stokes, from within the crease, tries to push at it tentatively. The ball hits the deck and moves away to beat Stoke's outside edge.
Shami keeps it a bit shorter of a length and outside off. Stokes lets it go. The ball, after crossing the batsman, moves prodigiously and Pant behind has to dive full length to his left to pouch it.
Starts the over with a very full delivery on off. Stokes leans forward and gently drives this to mid off.
Pitched up ball around off, Moeen stand his ground and blocks it.

That's  a jaffa! Keeps coming in with the natural around the wicket angle, squaring Ali up. Then the ball pitches and moves away to take the outside edge. It again falls short of gully. Kumar Dharmasena walks towards Ishant and has a word with him. Perhaps regarding him landing on the danger area. He needs to be careful.
Good length ball around that tight off stump channel, Ali presents a water-tight defense.
Full ball attacking the stumps, kept out watchfully.
Good probing stuff from Sharma! He bowls this one in the avenue of apprehension and gets it to move away a wee bit. Ali  points his bat skywards to allow it through.
In the zone outside off, Moeen lets it go.
A lot is happening at the moment! Pitched up ball around off, a lot of nibble in the air. Stokes pushes at it but gets an outside edge that lands just short of the crouching gully fielder.

Four Byes! That one moved a long way away! Outside off, Stokes lets it go. Pant dives full length but he has no chance to stop it. Pujara had to get out of the way as it was coming at a very brisk pace and he was not expecting it.

FOUR! Bumrah should have done better there. Fullish ball, too straight on this occasion. Stokes flicks it towards square leg. Bumrah stationed there dives lazily and allows the ball to roll past him and to the fence.
Ali is off the mark but not convincingly! On a length outside off, Moeen plays it with soft hands but gets it off the outer half past the gully region. Three runs taken.
Full but wide outside off this time, left alone.
Brilliant bowling! Shami switches to around the wicket and bowls a delivery that angles in sharply initially. At the last moment, it moves away as Ali leaves it tentatively.

Edged! Just short of third slip. Sharma lands it a bit fuller around off and shaping away. Stokes comes forward to block, gets a thick outside edge which goes straight to ground and on a bounce to Kohli at third slip. Stokes must have had his heart in his mouth a couple of times in this innings, but the important thing is, he's still out there and England desperately needs him to be.
Sharma probing away on the same line and length. Stokes gets behind the line of the ball and defends again.
Stokes defends this length ball on the middle and leg stump off the back foot.
Gets it fuller this time in the line of the stumps. Stokes waits for the ball to arrive and blocks it out.
Similar ball and blocked from the crease by Stokes.
Starts the over by landing it just short of a length on the middle stump line from around the wicket. Stokes gets behind and defends.
Whizzes past the edge. Shami has been probing nicely in the outside off stump channel. Ali hangs his bat looking to defend but misses.
Inswinger in line of the stumps, Stokes tucks the length ball to the on side and changes strike.
Too wide of off, Stokes keeps his bat away from the line of the ball.
On a length, outside off, left alone.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.

Bye! Nice stop from Pant. He has been agile today behind the sticks. A gentle loosener outside leg, Ali looks to flick but misses. Pant does well to dive to his right and stop the ball from going to the fine leg fence. The ball hits his glove and rolls to the on side as the batsmen take a run. The umpire signals a bye.
Sharma goes around the wicket and bowls a slower ball outside off and full. Stokes lunges forward to defend it but gets beaten. The ball goes to the keeper on a bounce. A nice tight over from Sharma.
And again. This is rigid from Stokes. He is leaving the angled ball on length and has been watchful of his off stump.
Stokes has no interest in playing the short deliveries around his off stump as he leaves another one for Pant for some practice.
Closer to the off pole on a similar length, Stokes leaves it seeing the away angle.
Again angles the length back across Stokes who lets it be.
Outside off, left alone.
Ishant Sharma is back on.

A bit shorter, attacking the line of the stumps. The ball pitches and seams into Ali who tries to work it away but misses and the ball raps him on his thigh pad. Shami generating some good pace and making life difficult for the English batsmen.
Length ball around off, Ali gets behind the line of the ball and blocks it out.
Bouncer from Shami, Ali ducks under it.
Moeen Ali walks in next.

OUT! Kohli takes a sharp one at third slip. England have lost half their side. Shami continues to land it in the corridor of uncertainty. Gets the ball to move away on pitching. Buttler, stuck in his crease, reaches out at the ball and goes for a drive on the up. This results in him getting the outside edge and the ball flies towards third slip at an awkward height. The Indian captain positioned there is alert and sharp enough to catch it sideways to his right. He made a sharp catch look easy, a mark of a good fielder. It should also be noted that after the four on the first ball of the over, Kohli removed the man at covers and got him in the gully position. The gap in the cover region tempted Buttler to go for the shot and the visitors are rewarded for some good thinking and better execution. In the last innings, Buttler had made the Indians pay for dropping him but he cannot capitalize this time around.
A bit wider outside off, shaping away. Buttler leaves it alone.

FOUR! Shot! A very full delivery by Shami is driven beautifully through covers by Buttler. He leans nicely into the drive, gets his head on top of the ball and demonstrates how to drive a swinging delivery.

FOUR! Stokes takes full toll of this loose one from Ashwin. He lands it a bit shorter outside off. Stokes rocks back and across and punches it off the back foot through the cover region. Finds the gap and the ball crosses the fence.
Tossed up outside off, Stokes shoulders arms.
Stokes dances down the track and does well to block the ball.
Shorter and wide by Ashwin, Stokes cuts it but the ball goes straight to the point fielder.
A bit slower, shorter and straighter from Ashwin. Stokes works it away off his pads.
Tossed up delivery is blocked off the front foot by Stokes.
Ashwin will bowl from the other end.
Length ball around off is defended of the front foot.

FOUR! Streaky!  That's the line Shami should hit consistently. Lands it a bit fuller on a length, it was on the middle stump line with some movement away. Buttler tries to push at it and gets squared up. The away movement takes the leading edge and the ball goes towards the backward point region for a boundary.
Outside off again and left again. Shami needs to make Buttler play.
Pulls the length just a wee bit and also comes a little closer to the off stump. However, Buttler seems to have a good idea where his off stump is and decides to leave it at the last moment.
Similar delivery and the same response from Buttler.
Starts the session with a full length ball, outside off and moving away. Buttler lets it go.
We are about to get the post-lunch session underway. The players and umpires are out in the middle. Mohammed Shami to start the proceedings for India. Let's see what's in store in this session...
... Day 1, Session 2 ...

The fourth wicket was the big one, of the other English opener and their highest scorer in Test cricket, Cook. It was a combination of some consistent bowling, a slight loss in concentration on the part of Cook and a brilliant low catch at third slip by the Indian captain. Since then, the pair of Stokes and Buttler has held the fort and has gone into lunch unbeaten. India will look to continue putting pressure on the English lower-order and try to wrap up the innings as early as possible. Stokes and Buttler, on the other hand, will look to build a long partnership and add some stability to the innings, similar to the way they fought back in the second innings at Trent Bridge. The post-lunch session starts in a while. Do join us.

What a great session for India, much better than what they would have expected after being asked to bowl. Their pacers were on the money from the very first ball. Jennings looked completely clueless when he left an incoming delivery from Bumrah and was caught plumb in front of the wickets.  The English skipper was lucky to survive a close LBW appeal against Bumrah, who again overstepped. But Sharma soon dismissed Root with a similar delivery, the only difference being, a part of his foot was behind the bowling crease. Bairstow was looking tentative until he got a beautiful delivery from Bumrah, almost an unplayable one.
Stokes again gets behind the line of the length ball to keep it out. That's Lunch on Day 1.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
An away swinging ball pitching outside the leg stump. Stokes fails to connect with the ball and gets hit high on his pads. An appeal ensues but the umpire ignores it.
Hangs back to show the full face and keeps it out down the ground.
Outside off, left alone.
On the pads, flicked through mid-wicket for a run.

An absolute peach this from Shami. He angles it across Stokes who looks to have a tentative push but misses. The ball gets some late swing and makes it troublesome for Pant behind the stumps once again. No harm done in the end. Last over before Lunch coming up next.
In line of the stumps, tucked to mid-wicket for a brace off the back foot.
Back of a length ball outside off, played through backward point for a run.

Dropped! A difficult one but it will be counted as a drop. Buttler survives once again, two chances in two Tests and Pant is the man again who gives him a reprieve. Shami digs this outside off and angles it into Buttler. He looks to leave it at the very last moment but the ball goes off the bottom half of the bat. Pant behind the stumps looks to get up with the bounce but the edge does him bad. It dips and goes on full to him. It hits him low on his leg and goes to the ground. Will Buttler make India pay once again?
Wide outside off stump, Buttler leaves it alone.
On a length, around off, left alone.
Ben chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Similar ball like 21.3 and same result as well. Stokes again comes walking down and is again beaten by the away movement. Could have easily edged this one but survives.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

Dear me. Out of 6 balls in an over, Bumrah bowls at least one unplayable ball just like this last one. A length ball pitching on middle and off and going across Stokes. He comes down the track to counter the swing but is beaten by the away movement. Geez!
Ben chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
A length ball angling across the left-hander who lets it be.
Jasprit Bumrah comes back on.
Takes a couple of steps down the track and seeing the short of a length, lets it pass. The ball swings in late and evades the diving Pant even though he dived to his right. A bye taken in the end.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Gets behind the line of this one and keeps it out.
A good comeback ball this. A full ball outside off and swinging in after pitching. Stokes doesn't fiddle with it.

Shami hasn't found his length this morning it seems. He bowls this one on the pads, Stokes flicks it through the backward square leg region and takes a brace. Shami cries 'C'mon yaar' as he sees Ashwin jogging to get to the ball.
Fuller on off, pushed to covers off the back foot by Stokes.
On off this time, on a similar length, Buttler blocks it under his eyes.
Shortish on middle and off, defended.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
FOUR! Another one. Two in two. A shortish ball in line of the stumps, Buttler clips it through square leg and the ball manages to cross the fence just in time.

FOUR! Drives and drives it nicely. A full length ball with some width on offer. Buttler's feet stays in his crease but his bat goes after it away from his body. The ball beats the cover fielder and races to the boundary.
Defended off the back foot by Jos.
Stokes wrists the length ball to the on side off his pads. A brace results.
Shows the full face of the bat and keeps it out off the front foot for no run.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Down the leg side, Stokes leaves it for the keeper. There is an appeal but the umpire ignores it.
Around off, left alone.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Leg Bye! An inswinging length ball in line of the stumps, Stokes looks to defend but the ball brushes his pads and rolls to the fine leg region. A run stolen.
Pandya errs in line a bit and dishes it on the hips. Buttler clips it fine and takes three before Dhawan cuts it out before reaching the boundary.
Similar length, outside off, Buttler lets it pass.
Outside off, left alone.
Fuller around off, driven to covers for no run.

OUT! Gone! Cook looks to fish around off and gets burned. Pandya is the man this time, the star of Nottingham, gets his name in the wicket's column in Southampton as well. A short of a length ball outside off, Cook probably looks to cut it through backward point off the back foot but ends up guiding it to Kohli at third slip. Kudos to the Indian skipper who stays low, crouches further down and takes a good catch to end Cook's gritty innings. Alastair will be disappointed as England are reeling at 36/4 now, just under 18 overs. Jos Buttler will be coming in to bat next.
Last ball of the over. Stokes leaves the length ball for the keeper. Not a bad start from Shami.
Flicks this length ball to the on side for no run.
A touch short, wide of off, Stokes slaps it through cover-point and takes a brace.
Around off, on a length, blocked.
Full, outside off, left alone.
Shami starts the proceedings with a short of a length ball in line of the stumps, Cook tucks it through mid-wicket off the inner half of the bat and changes strike.
Mohammed Shami comes in for a spell.
Shortish on middle and leg, Cook pushes it to the on side for no run.
Leg Bye! Full ball, on the pads, Stokes fails to put bat to ball and gets hit on his pads. A leg bye stolen by the batsmen.
In line of the stumps from Pandya, Stokes blocks it.
Around off, on a good length, defended.
Ben shoulders arms to let that one through.
FOUR! Shot! Played with such ease by Stokes. He gets a full ball on leg and flicks it from his crease. The connection is right and it goes through the vacant mid-wicket region for a boundary.
Straighter and fuller targeting the stumps, Cook comes on the front foot and defends.
On the off pole, solidly blocked off the front foot.
Watchful Cook once again defends the length ball right under his eyes.

This is a great leave. Too close to comfort but a great leave nonetheless. Cook leaves this one seeing that it pitched outside off. The ball moves in just a touch and goes past the off pole to the keeper.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Bumrah goes 'round the wicket to land this on a fuller length around off, Cook prods forward and gets it off the outer half of the bat.
On middle and off, Stokes keeps it out off the inner half of the bat.
In line of the stumps again, Stokes keep it out off the front foot for no run.
Ben has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
A shortish ball around off, Stokes lunges forward to get a thick outside edge. The ball lands in front of the fielder at third slip so no harm done.
On the pads, flicked to deep backward square leg for a run.
Pandya starts the spell with a length ball around off, Cook gets hit on his pad outside the line.
In comes Ben Stokes at number 5. Also, Hardik Pandya comes on for a bowl.

OUT! Bairstow can do nothing against this peach of a delivery from Bumrah. He lands this one on a length just outside off. Bairstow, after doing well in leaving these ones until now, is drawn into a defensive shot, may be because of Bumrah's angle and also the fact that this one is just that bit closer to the off stump. The ball pitches and straightens, the slight change in line gets the outside edge. It flies to Pant who pouches it and throws it high up in the air with delight. Bairstow has to take the long walk back. Interestingly, in the previous innings at Trent Bridge, Jonny was dismissed by Bumrah in a similar fashion.
Keeps it on a length outside off, Bairstow has nothing to do with it as he lets it go behind.
Bumrah strays on Cook's pads and he flicks it towards the square leg region for a single.
Cook shows the full face of the bat to defend this length delivery on off.
A bit shorter in length and in line with the stumps. Cooks walks across and tries to work it into the leg side but gets beaten to get rapped on the thigh pad.
Yorker to start the thirteenth over. Well dug out by Bairstow. The ball rolls down towards the square leg region and the batsmen take a quick single.

Drinks! A good start by India, picking up two English wickets, including their skipper. The Indian opening pace attack of Bumrah and Ishant have done well to keep the batsmen in check. They never let them get settled. The first hour belongs to the Indians.
Cook lets this length ball outside the off stump go behind.

Good stop by Rahane at short point. Ishant keeps this one fuller outside off stump. Cook goes for the drive but the ball moves away on landing and takes the outer half of his bat. The ball flies at a very low height towards Rahane at short point but falls way short of him. Rahane dives and saves four runs.
Similar delivery and Cook shoulders arms again.
Keeps it on a length but the line is way outside off for Cook to try any shot as he leaves it.
Ishant gets a bit straighter and strays it on his pads. Bairstow whips this one to the deep fine leg fielder for a single.
Starts the over with a length ball around off, the ball is shaping in nicely on pitching but Bairstow does well to account for the movement and blocks it solidly off the front foot.
Beaten again! Bumrah continues to land it on a length just outside off, Cook looking to block on the front foot but the ball pitches, nips away and beats the outside edge of his bat.
Yorker on off stump by Bumrah. Cook does well to dig it out in time.
Beaten! Bumrah keeps it on a length just outside off, Cook looks to defend but the ball pitches, nips away and beats his bat.
Very full delivery around off, Bairstow leans forward and drives this superbly through the covers. The fielder at covers gives a chase and keeps it down to three.
Fuller and straighter on middle and leg, Cook leans and works it into the mid-wicket region for a single.

Bumrah continues to trouble Cook. He lands it just short of a length around off stump from around the wicket. The ball lands and moves away a bit. Cook does not poke at it but the ball passes very near to the outside edge of his bat.
Wide down the leg side, Bairstow leaves it alone. Another good tight over from Sharma.

Goodness me, what a cracker. Sharma is looking so threatening, making the ball move so viciously. This one cut Bairstow in half. It lands on a back of a length and nips back in sharply. Bairstow is on the front foot and looks to play it with a lot of gap between ba and pad. The ball goes through the gap and over the sticks. Pant behind makes a diving stop with one hand to his left. Sharma can't believe it missed everything.
That ball has struck the batsman on the thigh pad.
Sharma is bowling a tad fuller this morning, making it hang in the air and letting it swing. The ball nips back in and Jonny manages to get an inside edge onto his pad.
An attempted bumper but the line is down the leg side. Pant makes a diving save to his left and saves runs for his team as Bairstow ducks under it.
Fuller outside off. Jonny pushes it tentatively to the off side.

Beaten! Another beautiful delivery by Bumrah. He angles this one into Cook on a length who tries to put bat on ball but it moves away after landing and beats the outside edge. A great delivery to end the over.
Fuller around off this time, Cook prods forward and defends.
Keeps it a bit short of a length. Cooks gets behind the line and blocks it.
FOUR! Cook does not miss out on this full toss wide of off stump. He reaches out and gets enough bat on this one, the ball races through the gap between gully and point and crosses the fence.
Lands it on a length, Cook comes forward to jab it away into the leg side.
The ball is too wide of the off stump to entice Cook into a shot.
A short of a length delivery on off, pitches and moves away a bit. Cook does well to account for the movement and pushes it towards the cover region. The batsmen run a single.
Gets a bit straighter this time as he lands this on middle and leg with the angle coming into the batsman, Bairstow works it away towards the mid-wicket region and changes strike.
On a good length around off, Bairstow defends off the front foot.
Bairstow chooses to leave this length delivery outside off.

Hits the pads again, India appeal again, but this time it's not out. Sharma keeps it a bit full on off, Bairstow comes forward to defend but gets hit on the pads. The ball is clearly missing the leg stump and Bairstow survives a golden duck.
Jonny Bairstow is the next batsman in.

OUT! Yes, it is plumb! India do get the English skipper. Bumrah must be a relieved man. Sharma continuing to bowl a bit fuller lands it just outside off. The ball hits the deck and nips back in. Root comes forward tentatively to block it out. Ishant's natural angle and the inward movement beats Root's inside edge and raps him, in what seems to be in front of the wickets. Kumar Dharmasena has no hesitation in giving it out. Root has a chat with Cook and decides to go for the review. The replay shows that the ball is hitting in line and there is no problem with the height as well as the ball is seen crashing into the stumps. What a wicket to have as your 250th Test scalp.
England this time take the review. Again it's Root, the man in question for another LBW appeal. It has been given out this time. He looks plumb. Let's wait for the replays.
Cook hangs back and keeps it out off the back foot to end the over. A rather good one for the home team.
FOUR! Bumrah errs in line and Cook makes him pay. He bowls a back of a length ball on the pads and Cook flicks it easily to the fine leg fence for his second boundary.
The batsman tries flicking a ball that is down the leg side but misses.
Too wide to entice Cook with a shot who lets it be.
Cook chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Leg Bye! Straightish on the hips, Root fails to get the flick as the ball hits his thigh pad and goes behind. A leg bye stolen.
Cook shoulders arms to this length ball wide outside off.

FOUR! That's the first boundary for England. Sharma keeps it a bit fuller and a bit wider of off. Cook leans forward and square drives this past the point fielder. The ball races across the boundary. Cook is hanging around for the sake of his team and putting the bad balls away.
Sharma attacks the line of the stumps, Cook gets behind the line of the ball and keeps it out.
A short of a length ball outside off is left alone.
Yorker! Sharma fires this one in the blockhole. Cook is alert enough to get his bat down in time. Good ball.
A length ball angled across Cook, he shoulders arms.
Bumrah keeps this length delivery in line of the stumps. Root, from his crease, defends it.
Root lets this one go outside the off stump.
Lands it on a good length just outside off, Root leaves.
Bumrah fires this on Root's pads who flicks this one into the leg side. The fielder at deep fine leg runs across and keeps it to two.

No ball. Bumrah does it again! He lands the ball on a length just outside off. Root hangs back looking to defend it. The ball pitches and seams in, beats Joe's bat and raps him dead in front. The Indians appeal but the umpire is unmoved. India, confidently go for the review. But but but, the first replay shows Bumrah has overstepped. The decision stays and Root survives a close, close call. Further replays also show that, with three reds, Joe would have been a goner. Bumrah's dreaded front foot again!
Review taken by India. Joe Root is the man in question and it's regarding an LBW decision.
Keeps it a bit fuller on off. Root comes forward and defends.
Length ball around off, defended off the back foot by Root.
Again around off, Cook leaves it for Pant behind the stumps.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Nice and watchful is Cook. He looks better today. Sharma is testing him out with a length ball pitched on off and going away after pitching. Cook blocks it off the front foot.
On a length this time, around off, Cook shoulders arms once again.
Similar kind of delivery from Sharma, asking Cook to have a go at it but he is not interested as he lets it pass.
Fullish length ball outside off, left alone.

Bumrah attacks the stumps, not a bad tactic. Root seemed to be a bit late on the shot but flicks it into the mid-wicket region at the last moment. The timing is not perfect and the mid on fielder keeps it down to two.
Keeps it just behind the length around off, Root comes right behind the line of the delivery and keeps it out.
Root shoulders arms to this length ball outside off.

Beaten! Root sees the initial line of the delivery coming into him from around the off stump, tries to block it but the ball nips away on landing to beat the outside edge. The slip cordon have their hands on their heads as the English captain survives.
Lands it on a length just outside off. Root comes forward and defends solidly.
Joe Root walks out to the middle.

OUT! What a jaffa! Boom Boom Bumrahhh! Dream start for India as they draw first blood. He lands this one on a length on middle and off stump. Jennings expecting the ball to continue with the angle, shoulders his arms but the ball pitches and moves in prodigiously. Hits Jennings on the inside part of his front pad in front of the stumps. The Indians appeal and the umpire has no hesitation in giving this out. A big error in judgement has cost Jennings his wicket. Bumrah will now have his tail up.
Cook goes back to this short of a length ball on off and keeps it out.
On a length outside off, Cook shoulders arms.
Ishant pulls the length back a bit. Cook gets behind the line of the ball and defends.
Cook shoulders arms to this length ball outside off.

Beaten! He's genuinely beaten here. Sharma lands it on a length on off from around the wicket. The ball pitches and nips away from Cook who has a tentative poke at the ball. The outside edge is beaten and Cook survives.
Sharma starts on a length just outside off. Cook leaves.
Ishant Sharma will bowl from the other end.
Jennings shoulders arms to this length ball outside off to end the first over.

Beaten! Bumrah's angle doing the talking here. He lands this on a length on middle and off, Jennings sees the initial line and tries to put bat on ball. But the movement away after pitching beats his outside edge.
Keeps it just behind a length on the off stump, Jennings lets this one go past him.
Tries to compensate on the line and strays on the batsman's pads, Cook gets inside the line and tucks it from his hips to the man at deep fine leg. England are underway.
Lands this one on a length on off stump, the ball goes across Cook who shoulders arms.

Starts the match with a peach of a delivery. Lands it on a short of a length, on middle and off, Bumrah's angle takes the ball across Cook and the ball whizzes past the outside edge. Good start by Bumrah.
Three slips and a gully for Jasprit Bumrah, who will open the bowling for the tourists. Here we go...

Right, so the fourth Test of this series is about to get underway. The players and umpires walk out to the middle. Alastair Cook and Keaton Jennings stride out. The former will face the music first up.

India captain, Virat Kohli says that he wanted to bat first as well. He reckons that the pitch looks good for batting. Implies that it looks hard and in the first 20-25 minutes, they will look to extract something out of it. Further adds that for the first time in a long time, they are going with an unchanged squad. Asserts that there are some niggles but those have been neglected. Further says that Ravichandran Ashwin is fit so there was no need to make any changes. Asserts that the players are waiting for the opportunities rather than being unaware of them. Ends by saying that his team is experienced as compared to the one in 2014 and will look to work hard even more and put in a good performance.

England captain, Joe Root says that he wants to take advantage of the pitch. Adds that there are some changes as Chris Woakes is injured so Sam Curran replaces him and Moeen Ali comes in as well in place of Ollie Pope as he has played some great cricket in the last couple of weeks. Further adds that Moeen Ali is a good player and he will be looking to make things work. Implies that Jonny Bairstow has some niggle but he will be fine to bat at number four. Ends by saying that after Trent Bridge, they are looking to set things right.
Toss - England win the toss and will bat.

Pitch Report - Sanjay Manjrekar reports from the pitch and states that it looks flawless, the best one of the series so far. Feels that there is nothing to suggest any uneven pace or bounce. Mentions there is an even covering of grass throughout the surface. Reckons some dryness might come into play after the first couple of days. Admits that the opening batsmen will have their work cut out in the first hour or two, when the ball may do a bit. Reckons the captain who wins the toss should bat first. Ends by saying that the pitch looks to be in excellent condition and expects to be an exciting contest between bat and ball.

Hola! We're here at Rose Bowl, Southampton for the fourth Test between England and India. After two one-sided and one closely fought Test, it's time for the fourth game of the Pataudi series. The contest still favours the hosts but the tide has been changing slowly but surely. England have made a few changes to the playing XI with Sam Curran and Moeen Ali coming in for Ollie Pope and Chris Woakes. For the visitors, their side looks settled and there doesn't seem to be any need for changes. However, Virat Kohli has been known to make changes in each of the Tests he has led. It's sunny for now and there are some predictions of weather turning overcast during the day. Anyhow, it promises to be a cracker of a contest once again. The action starts in a while, hang around!
